questions.stem: A 36-year-old female presented to emergency with cough, fever, and abdominal and back pain for one week. She had tachycardia, tachypnoea, hypotension and bilateral rales on auscultation. Chest radiographs revealed rounded densities in the right middle lung. Initial assessment of the chest radiographs signified acute respiratory failure with severe sepsis, likely secondary to pneumonia. The patient was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation, started on vasopressors, antibiotics, propofol and midazolam for sedation. Her condition worsened and that resulted in increased doses of all sedative agents and the addition of fentanyl. 2-3 days later, she developed generalized rash over the body along with elevated Creatinine, sinus tachycardia, diastolic dysfunction and metabolic acidosis. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.stemHtml: A 36-year-old female presented to emergency with cough, fever, and abdominal and back pain for one week. She had tachycardia, tachypnoea, hypotension and bilateral rales on auscultation. Chest radiographs revealed rounded densities in the right middle lung. Initial assessment of the chest radiographs signified acute respiratory failure with severe sepsis, likely secondary to pneumonia. The patient was intubated and placed on mechanical ventilation, started on vasopressors, antibiotics, propofol and midazolam for sedation. Her condition worsened and that resulted in increased doses of all sedative agents and the addition of fentanyl. 2-3 days later, she developed generalized rash over the body along with elevated Creatinine, sinus tachycardia, diastolic dysfunction and metabolic acidosis. What is the likely diagnosis?

options.label: C
options.text: Respiratory Failure due to Over Sedation
